{{nihongo|'''Yagawa Shrine'''|矢川神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Ōmi Province]].

'''Yagawa Shrine''' (やがわじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Kōnan-chō Morijiri|Q86735490|qid=Q86735490}}, {{ill|Kōka, Shiga|Q847584|qid=Q847584}}, {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|Q131358|qid=Q131358}}.

=== Enshrined deities ===
The principal deities are {{ill|Ōkuninushi|Q276944|qid=Q276944|lt=Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto}} and Yagawa-e-hime-no-Mikoto<ref>{{Cite web|和書|title=Yagawa Shrine|url=http://www.shiga-jinjacho.jp/ycBBS/Board.cgi/02_jinja_db/db/ycDB_02jinja-pc-detail.html?mode:view=1&view:oid=613|website=|accessdate=2019-10-24|publisher=Shiga Prefecture Shrine Office}}</ref>. Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto is revered as a deity of industry and long healthy life; Yagawa-e-hime-no-Mikoto as a deity for mastery of arts and fulfillment of wishes.

Yagawa-e-hime-no-Mikoto is also written as Yagawae-hime / Yagawae-hime. In the genealogy of Ōkuninushi in the {{ill|Kojiki|Q813031|qid=Q813031}}, there is a passage: "{{ill|Kuninotoshimi-no-Kami|Q48759713|qid=Q48759713}} married {{ill|Ashinataka-no-Kami|Q55533749|qid=Q55533749}} (also called Yagawae-hime), and their child was {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Hayamika-no-Takesawaya-jinumi-no-Kami}}." Also, in the {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|Q317997|qid=Q317997}} section of the Kojiki, Miyanushi Yagawae-hime appears as one of the emperor's consorts.

=== History ===
Shrine tradition says it was founded in the {{ill|Tenpyō|Q1199879|qid=Q1199879}} era, during construction of {{ill|Shigaraki Palace|Q262438|qid=Q262438}} by {{ill|Emperor Shōmu|Q349263|qid=Q349263}}. In the {{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}} '{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}},' it appears first among eight shrines of Kōka District, {{ill|Ōmi Province|Q843882|qid=Q843882}}, and is listed as a small shrine. A 1337 source from the {{ill|Nanboku-chō period|Q264012|qid=Q264012}} records it as "Soma-no-Kawa-no-Miya," and in the medieval period it gathered support from local warrior-landholders as the sōsha of Ikebara Soma-shō<ref name=":0" />. In the {{ill|Sengoku period|Q204023|qid=Q204023}}, it was used as a meeting place of the {{ill|Kōka ikki|Q85882491|qid=Q85882491}}, functioning as a site strengthening regional cohesion<ref name=":1" />. After the decline of Kōka groups in the {{ill|Kōga-ryū|Q6455112|qid=Q6455112}} of {{ill|1585|Q6736|qid=Q6736}}, ritual structure changed. In {{ill|1652|Q6962|qid=Q6962}}, among ujiko villages, 9 villages became ujiko of Shingū Shrine ({{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kōnan-chō Shinjī}}), 6 villages became ujiko of Hiyoshi Shrine ({{ill|Minakuchi-chō Sandaiji|Q86735520|qid=Q86735520}}), and 7 villages (Morijiri, Fukagawa, Hietani, Kuzuraki, Terashō, Sugitani, Shiono) remained ujiko (Yagawa Hongō / Yagawa 7 villages), while another 15 villages were called external ujiko<ref name=":0" />. In the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, it was a revered shrine of {{ill|Minakuchi Domain|Q10863504|qid=Q10863504}}. In October {{ill|Tenpō|Q1369045|qid=Q1369045}} 13 ({{ill|1842|Q7625|qid=Q7625}}), the "Kōka Disturbance" ({{ill|Tenpō uprising|Q11638484|qid=Q11638484|lt=Tenpō uprising}}) occurred at this shrine precinct, where tens of thousands of farmers gathered and rose against shogunate land survey policy.

Before Meiji it was called Yagawa Daimyōjin and was a broad-area village guardian shrine with a wide ujiko sphere<ref name=":0">{{Cite book|title=Kōka City History Vol.8 Kōka City Encyclopedia|date=2016年12月12日|year=2016|publisher=Kōka City|pages=171-172}}</ref>. Rituals were carried out under {{ill|Shinbutsu-shūgō|Q2279088|qid=Q2279088}} by Yagawadera Seijō-in, the shrine's {{ill|Jingū-ji|Q1074971|qid=Q1074971}} (now extinct)<ref name=":0" />.

=== National historic site ===
Precincts - designated as a national historic site as one of the {{ill|Kōka ikki|Q85882491|qid=Q85882491|lt=Kōka-gun Chūsō site group}}<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite journal|author=Kōka City|year=2009|title=Understanding the real figure of Kōka warriors who raced through the Sengoku period|url=http://www.city.koka.lg.jp/secure/6711/2009_0601_p02_03.pdf|journal=Kōhō Aikōka|volume=June 1 issue|page=}}</ref>.

=== Cultural properties ===
=== Prefecture-designated cultural properties ===
* Rōmon gate - said to have been donated in thanks for rainmaking fulfilled for 50 villages in {{ill|Yamabe District, Nara|Q1130739|qid=Q1130739}}, {{ill|Yamato Province|be|Ямата (правінцыя)|ca|Província de Yamato|ckb|پارێزگای یەماتۆ|cs|Provincie Jamato|de|Provinz Yamato|el|Επαρχία Γιαμάτο|es|Provincia de Yamato|fa|ولایت یاماتو|fi|Yamaton provinssi|fr|Province de Yamato|gl|Provincia de Yamato|hak|Yamato-koet|id|Provinsi Yamato|it|Yamato (provincia)|ja|大和国|ko|야마토국|lt|Jamato žemė|nl|Yamato (provincie)|no|Yamato (provins)|pt|Província de Yamato|ro|Provincia Yamato|ru|Ямато (провинция)|simple|Yamato Province|sk|Jamato (provincia)|sr|Провинција Јамато|th|แคว้นยามาโตะ|tr|Yamato (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Ямато|ur|یاماتو صوبہ|zh|大和國|zh_min_nan|Yamato-kok|zh_yue|大和國|qid=Q907495}} (northern {{ill|Nara Prefecture|Q131287|qid=Q131287}}). Originally two-storied, but said to have lost the upper story to weather. Built in {{ill|1482|Q6633|qid=Q6633}}<ref name=":0" />.
* Paper, light-color paintings "Immortals with game board books" and "Landscape" - by {{ill|Yokoi Kinkoku|Q3122882|qid=Q3122882}}.

=== City-designated cultural properties ===
* Honden - sangen-sha nagare-zukuri with steel-sheet roof. Rebuilt in {{ill|1755|Q7627|qid=Q7627}} by Takagi Tajima, a carpenter from Hachiman<ref name=":0" />.
* Stone arched bridge (taiko-bashi) - built in {{ill|1671|Q7610|qid=Q7610}}. Oldest stone arched bridge in Kōka<ref>{{Cite book|title=Kōka City History Vol.8 Kōka City Encyclopedia|date=2016年12月12日|year=2016|publisher=Kōka City|page=389}}</ref> and largest<ref name=":0" />.
* Wooden male deity statue - Heian-period work.

=== Other ===
* Wooden female deity statue - Heian-period work<ref name=":0" />.
